cases.headline: Breakdown (shadow short) in a Weak market
cases.bull:
**Bull case (for the short), stated honestly: it is real but weaker than the grade suggests.**

**Trend and stage.** This is a clean downtrend. Close 970.6 is 19.8% below the 50-day SMA and 26.5% below the 200-day. The stock is 40.6% off its 52-week high, with ret_63 of -36.3% against a benchmark +1.8%. Mansfield is -28.85, RS rank is 5, and the market regime is Weak (benchmark below a falling 200-day, stage-2 share 48.5%). The sector is soft too: only 38% of Financial Services names are advancing, and the 63-day sector median is -4.8%. The stock is falling much faster than its sector.

**Base and break.** The 17-day base had a pivot at 993.9, which was the 10-26 low. Today's low of 965.7 and close of 970.6 break it decisively. The rally to 1,110 on 11-17 failed, and 11-18 fell to 1,046, so the stock rolled over from a lower high.

**Volume.** Volume was 1.35M, 4.33x the norm, on a -7.2% day. That is real distribution, not a drift through support. The weekly bar is also a wide-range bearish close at its low.

**Stop and target.** The stop at 1,076.42 is 10.9% above entry, which is about 2.5 ATR. It sits above the 11-18 breakdown area and the 11-17 high of 1,115, so a close back above it would invalidate the break. At 0.5% risk, that means roughly Rs 4,600 of position on a Rs 1 lakh account. A target near 800-850 (a measured move of roughly the 16% base depth) gives about 1.5R or better.

**Honest weakness.** The screen's own record does not support the signal: same-grade n=98 shows avg R -0.30 and 47% wins; same grade and regime n=68 shows -0.43 and 40%; the most similar n=25 shows -0.40. The stock is already 20.9% down in 21 days and sits only 0.5% above its 52-week low, so this is a stretched, late entry prone to snap-back bounces, as seen after 10-23. The one similar prior case (n=1) stopped out in a session.

**What proves me wrong:** a close above 1,076, or a quick recovery above the 993.9 pivot on falling volume.
cases.bear:
As the Bear, my case is that the breakdown short is a poor trade for this account, mainly because it is late and the stop is wide.

**Extended and late.** The stock is already 40.6% below its 52-week high and 19.8% below its 50-day average. It is down 36.3% over 63 days and 20.9% over 21 days, against a benchmark that gained 1.8% over 63 days. Mansfield is -28.85 and RS rank is 5. The weakness is real, but the easy part of the move is behind us. Today's close of 970.6 sits just 0.5% above the 52-week low, so the entry is at the bottom of a capitulation-style leg. Volume of 1.35M was 4.33x normal, and the 3.3M volume on 10-23 looked like a washout. Climactic volume near lows often marks exhaustion, not the start of a new leg. The prior bounce from 993.9 to 1151 on 11-05 shows buyers appear at this level.

**Stop too wide.** The stop is 1076.42, 10.9% above entry. With ATR at 4.36%, that is about 2.5 ATR. A 21-session hold needs a further sharp fall to pay for that risk. At 0.5% risk on Rs 1 lakh (Rs 500), the position is only about Rs 4,600 notional, which is tiny. It is also a delivery-only account, so a short is not even directly executable, which makes this a shadow trade.

**Track record is negative.** The screen's history on this grade has n=98, average R -0.3, and 47% wins. In the same regime the figures are n=68, average R -0.43, and 40% wins. The most similar cases (n=25) show average R -0.4 and median return -1.1%. The screen has not shown an edge. One similar judged case, a shadow short in a Weak regime, hit its stop in 1 session (R -1.08). That is n=1, so it is weak evidence, but it points the same way.

**Context.** The sector is mixed, with 38% advancing but a median 21-day return of +1.7%. VIX is 16.1, which is calm, so there is no panic tailwind. The next results date is unknown, which is itself a gap-risk unknown.

**What would change my mind:** a failed bounce that stays under about 1,050 on falling volume, or a close below 965 that holds, would show real continuation. A smaller position with a tighter stop would also help.

judge.title: Avoid
judge.text: The stock is in a steep downtrend. It closed at 970.6, about 20% below its 50-day average and 26% below its 200-day, and 40.6% under its 52-week high. It sat in a 17-day range above 993.9 and broke below it today with a 7% drop on 4.33 times normal volume, closing only 0.5% above its 52-week low. It has lost 36% in three months while the index gained 1.8% and the median financial-services stock fell 4.8%, so it is far weaker than both.
reasons_for: The breakdown below the 993.9 pivot came on 4.33x normal volume, a -7.2% day, after a lower high near 1,110 on 11-17.
Relative weakness is extreme: RS rank 5, Mansfield -28.85, ret_63 -36.3% against a benchmark +1.8%.
The market regime is Weak, with the benchmark not above a rising 200-day SMA and only 38% of sector members advancing.
reasons_against: The screen's own history is negative: same grade n=98, avg R -0.30, 47% wins; same grade and Weak regime n=68, avg R -0.43, 40% wins; most similar n=25, avg R -0.40. Nothing here shows this case differs.

The entry is late and stretched: down 20.9% in 21 sessions, 19.8% below the 50-day SMA, and just 0.5% above the 52-week low. The last washout on 10-23 (3.3M shares) bounced from about 994 to 1,151 within two weeks.
The stop at 1076.42 is 10.9% away, about 2.5 ATR at an ATR of about 42.3. A Rs 500 risk therefore buys only about Rs 4,600 of exposure, and a snap-back like the one in early November would hit it.
The account is delivery-only, so it cannot hold a short for 1-3 months. The only similar judged shadow short (n=1, Weak regime) stopped out in 1 session at -1.08R.
judge.invalidation: The short case fails on a daily close back above the 993.9 pivot that holds, and is decisively wrong on a close above 1076.42. Only a sustained close below about 965 after a failed bounce under 1,050 would make a breakdown short worth revisiting.

cases.headline: Breakdown (shadow short) in a Weak market
cases.bull:
**Bull case for the short (breakdown) in POLYCAB.NS, honestly stated**

**Important constraint:** the account is delivery-only, so an actual short isn't executable. This is a shadow signal. The case below is for the signal's merit, and the practical outcome is probably "avoid or stay out of the long side."

**Trend and stage:** The stock is clearly in decline. It closed at 7307.5, which is 9.4% below the 50-day SMA, 13.5% below the 200-day SMA, and 27.8% off the 52-week high. It fell from about 10,083 on 19 June. Returns are -11.1% over 21 days and -22.0% over 63 days, against a benchmark 63-day return of +0.3%. Mansfield is -13.74 and RS rank is 26. The screen labels it Stage 3 Topping.

**Breakdown quality:** The close sits below the 7372.5 pivot, which was the 23 October low. The day's range was 7293 to 7670, and it closed near the low. Volume was 864k, about 2.0x average. The base is 17 sessions long and 12% deep, a reasonable consolidation to break.

**Context:** The market regime is Weak, and the benchmark is below a falling 200-day SMA. Sector median returns are negative (-4.3% over 21 days, -9.4% over 63 days), so the stock isn't fighting its group.

**Base rates:** The most-similar subset (n=25) shows average R of +0.22, a 56% win rate and +1.7% average excess return. That is a small n, so it is weak evidence. The broader same-grade (n=98, -0.3R) and same-grade-and-regime (n=68, -0.43R) results are negative, and they are the larger samples. I can't lean on the favourable one.

**Levels:** Entry is 7307.5 and the stop is 7927.32, a risk of 619.8, or 8.5%. A target of about 6700 to 6850, near the April and March lows, gives roughly 1:1. That is not attractive.

**What proves me wrong:** A close back above 7670 (the breakdown day's high), and especially above the 7927 stop, which is roughly where the 12 November rally failed. A sharp bounce after a 3.4% ATR day also hurts. The one similar closed case stopped out within a session.

Honest verdict: the trend case is real, but the wide stop, the poor 1:1 reward and the unexecutable delivery-only short make this weak.
cases.bear:
Bear case against acting on this short in POLYCAB.NS (entry 7307.5, stop 7927.32):

**This is a delivery-only account, so a short can't be executed as signalled.** A retail Indian account holding delivery cannot carry a short for one to three months. The signal is shadow-only, and the most that can honestly be done is avoid the stock.

**The screen has not shown an edge.** Same-grade history is n=98, avg R -0.30, win 47%, median return -0.4%. Same grade and Weak regime is n=68, avg R -0.43, win 40%. Only the "most similar" subset looks good (n=25, avg R +0.22, win 56%), but that is a small sample, matched on five fields and likely flattered by tuning. I would not lean on it. The one closed judged case, a similar Weak-regime short, hit its stop in one session (-1.08R). That is n=1, but it shows how these setups fail.

**The move is already extended.** Price is 9.4% below the 50-day average, 13.5% below the 200-day, down 11.1% in 21 days and 22.0% in 63 days. The entry sits 10.2% above the 52-week low, so there is little room before the obvious support. The pivot at 7372.5 is the 2026-10-23 low (7372.5). Today closed at 7307.5, just below it, and a quick reclaim would be a classic failed breakdown. Last month's bounce from 7440 to 8080 (11/12) shows sharp rallies do occur here.

**The stop is wide.** The stop is 620 points, 8.5% above entry, against a 21-session hold. With ATR at 3.39% (about 248), that is roughly 2.5 ATR. Reward to the 52-week low area is small relative to that risk, and sizing at 0.5% risk would be tiny.

**Context cuts both ways.** Volume ratio 2.02 and a bar closing near its low (high 7670, low 7293, close 7307.5) support the short. But the weak market (regime Weak, VIX 15.52, benchmark 63-day return +0.28%) is already priced into a stock with RS rank 26 and Mansfield -13.74. Sector median 63-day return is -9.4%, so this is partly sector beta, and the stock's -22.0% is not far beyond it.

**What would change my mind:** a second close below 7293 on volume, and a failed bounce below roughly 7700.

judge.title: Avoid
judge.text: Polycab has been falling since its June peak near 10,083. It now sits at 7307.5, 27.8% below its 52-week high and 13.5% under its 200-day average. On 18 Nov it closed just under the 7372.5 low of a 17-session base, near the bottom of the day's range, on about 2x normal volume. That is a genuine breakdown. Over 63 days the stock fell 22%, while the index gained 0.3% and the Industrials sector median fell 9.4%, so it is weak both on its own and against the market.
reasons_for: The trend is clearly down: price is -9.36% below the 50-day SMA, -13.45% below the 200-day, with a 63-day return of -22.0% against a benchmark at +0.28%.
The breakdown bar is decent: it closed at 7307.5 below the 7372.5 pivot, near the 7293 low, on a volume ratio of 2.02.
The backdrop is unhelpful for longs: the market regime is Weak, the benchmark is not above a rising 200-day, and the sector's 63-day median is -9.37%.
reasons_against: The account is delivery-only and cannot carry a short for 21 to 63 sessions, so the signal cannot be acted on.

The screen has no proven edge on this side: same grade gives n=98, avg -0.30R, 47% wins; same grade in a Weak regime gives n=68, avg -0.43R, 40% wins. Only the small most-similar subset (n=25, +0.22R) is positive.
The screen's stop at 7927.32 is 620 points (8.5%, about 2.5 ATR of 248) away, while the 52-week low is only about 10.2% below. That leaves a poor reward for the risk.
The stock has already fallen far, and rallies here are sharp: it ran from 7440 to 8080 in 3 weeks in late October and November, so a failed breakdown is a real risk.
The one similar judged Weak-regime short (n=1) hit its stop within a single session at -1.08R.
judge.invalidation: For this shadow short, a daily close back above 7670 (the breakdown day's high), and certainly above 7700, marks the breakdown below the 7372.5 pivot as failed. The screen's own stop at 7927.32 is where the 12 Nov rally faded.

cases.headline: Breakdown (shadow short) in a Weak market
cases.bull:
**Case for acting on the short signal (Bull = pro-signal), stated honestly.**

**Trend and stage:** This is a textbook Stage 4 decline. The close of 517.75 sits 14.9% below the 50-day SMA and 31.8% below the 200-day. It is 56% off the 52-week high and 0.34% above the 52-week low, so it is at the low. Returns are negative at every horizon: 21d -12.0%, 63d -28.5%, 126d -38.9%, 252d -55.6%. The benchmark's 63-day return is +0.4%, so the stock is falling on its own, not with the market.

**Relative strength:** The RS rank is 3 and the Mansfield reading is -35.84. That is near the bottom of the universe.

**Volume and breakdown:** The signal bar is decisive. It opened at 558, made a low of 516, and closed at 517.75 on 157,911 shares. That is about 4.7x the volume ratio and the largest volume in the whole daily series, bar the 225k on 5/25. It closed at the low of the day, 8.6% below the prior close of 566.5. It also broke the 524 pivot, the 10/23 low, on heavy volume. The 11/2 to 11/12 bounce stalled at a 597.6 high, a lower high, which is consistent with supply.

**Market context:** The regime is Weak, the benchmark is below a rising 200-day, and only 47.6% of stocks are in Stage 2. That backdrop is mildly supportive of a short.

**Stop and target:** The screen's stop is 571.13, 10.3% above entry. That is a wide stop, about 2.5x ATR (ATR is 4.1%), and it sits above the 11/13 close of 566.5, so a recovery of the whole bounce would be needed to hit it. A 21-session target near 450 to 470 (a measured move from the 524 to 597 range) would give roughly 1.2 to 1.6R.

**Honest weaknesses:** The track record is poor. For the same grade, n=361 gives avg R -0.29 and a 43% win rate. For same grade and regime, n=279 gives avg R -0.46 and a 38% win rate. The most similar cases (n=25) have a median R of 0.01 and a 52% win rate, which is too small to lean on. The stock is also extended after a 12% fall in 21 days, so a bounce is likely. Also, this is a delivery-only account, so an actual short may not be executable.

**What would prove me wrong:** A close back above 566.5, or a reclaim of 524 on volume. Any close above 571.13 is a failed breakdown.
cases.bear:
The short is a poor risk for a Rs 1 lakh delivery-only account, and the screen's own history says so.

**Base rates.** Past shorts from this screen with the same grade lost money: n=361, average R -0.29, median -0.19, win rate 43%, average excess return -1.0%. In the same weak regime they did worse: n=279, average R -0.46, win rate 38%. The most similar cases (n=25) are a coin flip, with a 52% win rate and a median R of 0.01. That n is too small to lean on, and it still shows no edge. The screen's grades were also tuned on this history, so the real figures are probably worse.

**Delivery-only.** The pack gives no way to short in delivery. Indian retail cannot hold a short for one to three months without futures, and this pack does not show whether any derivative exists on this stock. The signal may not be tradeable as written.

**Extended and late.** The close of 517.75 is 56% below the 52-week high and 0.34% above the 52-week low. It is 31.8% under the SMA200 and 14.9% under the SMA50. The 252-day return is -55.6% and the 126-day return is -38.9%. Selling the low of a long decline invites a snapback. The stock bounced from 538 to 588 in early November, about 9%, before this drop.

**Capitulation volume.** Volume on the signal day was 157,911, against a typical 15,000-50,000. The vol_ratio is 4.74. A 7% drop to a 52-week low on a volume spike often marks exhaustion rather than the start of a leg. The close sits near the low, which is bearish, but the entry is also the worst price in the move.

**Stop and reward.** The stop is 571.13, 53.38 points or 10.3% above entry. That is wide against a 4.1% ATR. At 0.5% risk, the position is only about Rs 48,500 in notional. A 21-session hold needs a further drop of over 10% just to reach 1R, and one rebound day like 11 Nov (+3.5%) cuts into that.

**What supports the short.** Stage 4, an RS rank of 3, a Mansfield of -35.8, a Weak regime and a benchmark below its SMA200 are all bearish. They are already priced into the screen's poor outcomes.

**What would change my mind:** a failed bounce that stays under about 540, falling volume on the rebound, and confirmation that the short can actually be held for weeks.

judge.title: Avoid
judge.text: The stock has been falling steadily for a year. It is down 55.6% over 252 days and now sits just 0.34% above its 52-week low and 31.8% below its 200-day average. It tried to bounce in early November, reaching 597.6, then broke under its 524 low on 16 Nov with a 7-9% drop on about 4.7 times normal volume, closing at the day's low. It is far weaker than the index, with a 63-day return of -28.5% against +0.4% for the benchmark and an RS rank of 3. No sector data is given.
reasons_for: Clear Stage 4 decline: the close of 517.75 is 14.9% below the 50-day SMA and 31.8% below the 200-day, with negative returns at every horizon (21d -12.0%, 252d -55.6%).
Relative strength is near the bottom: RS rank 3 and Mansfield -35.84, while the benchmark gained 0.4% over 63 days.
The breakdown bar closed at its low (516 low, 517.75 close) and broke the 524 pivot on a 4.74x volume ratio, after a lower high of 597.6.
The market regime is Weak, the benchmark is not above a rising SMA200, and the Stage 2 share is only 47.6%.
reasons_against: The screen's own base rates are negative. Same grade: n=361, avg R -0.29, win rate 43%. Same grade and Weak regime: n=279, avg R -0.46, win rate 38%. Most-similar cases: n=25, median R 0.01, too small a sample and still no edge.
The account is delivery-only, so a 21-63 session short cannot be held in cash equity. The signal is not executable as written.

The entry is 0.34% above the 52-week low after a 28.5% fall in 63 days. A volume spike of 157,911 shares, against a typical 15-50k, can be capitulation that invites a snapback like the earlier 538 to 597.6 bounce.
The stop at 571.13 is 53.38 points (10.3%, about 2.5 ATR at a 4.12% ATR) above entry. A 1.5R target needs a further drop to about 435, roughly another 16%, within the holding window.
judge.invalidation: The short case fails on any close above 571.13. A close back above 566.5 (the 11/13 close), with the 524 pivot reclaimed, would mark the breakdown as a failed capitulation.
